news.title: Cafu On India-Brazil Match And Football's Future
news.lede: Legendary Brazilian footballer Cafu shares insights on India's football development, Brazil's World Cup aspirations, and the evolving dynamics of the sport ahead of India's historic friendly against the five-time champions. Former Brazil captain Cafu on Friday said the Indian team will learn a lot from its first-ever international match against his country in Kolkata next month, though he admitted to the significant gap in the rankings between the two countries. news.title: World Cup Players Drive Record $3.3 Billion in Transfer Fees
news.lede: FIFA has revealed that players who featured in the 2026 World Cup were a major catalyst for record-breaking international transfer fees, generating over $3.3 billion during the recent mid-year window and contributing to an unprecedented $9.89 billion spent in men's football. Players who featured at the 2026 World Cup generated more than $3.3 billion in international transfer fees during the recently concluded mid-year transfer window, FIFA said on Thursday. More than 260 World Cup players from 47 nationalities changed clubs during the window, accounting for over a third of the record $9.89 billion spent on international transfer fees in men's football, according to soccer's global governing body. "More than 12,500 international transfers were registered around the world, also setting a new record for the number of transfers during a mid-year window," FIFA said in a study.

news.lede: FIFA has accused the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) of pursuing a “smear campaign” and a “fishing expedition” after the European governing body asked US judges to compel the global football body to release documents linked to its abandoned World Cup investment plan. UEFA had threatened to boycott the World Cup if FIFA proceeded with the plan, intensifying pressure on the global governing body to abandon the proposal.

news.title: Poland and Ukraine set sights on future World Cup
news.lede: Poland and Ukraine are considering a joint bid to host a future men's FIFA World Cup, reviving a partnership that staged the 2012 European Championship. Ukrainian Sports Minister Matvii Bidnyi told POLITICO that Kyiv was interested in exploring a joint bid with the next available World Cup slot expected to be in the 2040s. “The nearest open date for the World Cup is somewhere in the 2040s … so we need to plan for this perspective right now,” Bidnyi said. But Poland's Ministry of Sport and Tourism told TVP World on Friday that it was not holding talks with Ukraine about hosting the tournament, contradicting reports of discussions over a potential joint bid.
